breakdown.method: Batch score = lowest page score (07-judge.md; config pass_threshold 90); a page scores as its lowest key. Each key was scored on five axes: accuracy 30, nativeness 30, termbase/transliteration/orthography 20, fit for the Urdu-speaking traveller 10, structure 10. The axes below are the minima of the lowest keys (tmap.gest.win and tmap.gest.mac, 91). The blind reader's page marks (A 68, B 74, C 72, D 55, overall 64) are a reading, not the score: 25 of its 51 items fall on published Urdu or reading-tool artefacts outside this batch, and 22 of the rest are ruled against the sources and the rulings that bind.

The third reader's 'serious' charge (#31: the phrase is mostly figurative) is the charge of two earlier readers (b21-ui, N333 round 2) and the answer is the same plus new evidence. (1) The physical sense is attested in running text: ur.wikipedia «سطح مرتفع پوٹھوہار» («اس کی سطح مسلسل نشیب و فراز رکھتی ہے … وادیاں، ندی نالے»), «چندریان-2» («چاند کی سطح کے نشیب و فراز کا ڈیجیٹل نقشہ تیار کیا جائے گا» — a relief map, the very object), «قیامت» («زمین میں … نشیب و فراز، وادیاں، کہسار اور پہاڑ»). (2) «تضاریسی» (the reader's second candidate) has no attestation: ur.wikipedia exact phrases «تضاریسی نقشہ» 0 pages and «تضاریس» 0 pages (HTTP 200), a technical Arabic loan a Urdu reader would meet less than the Persian compound; the Rekhta pages tried answered 503 and are not counted. (3) «زمین کی اونچ نیچ» 0 pages (HTTP 200); bare «اونچ نیچ» 34 pages, whose top titles include «اونچ نیچ بیچ» and «جنوبی ایشیا کے روایتی کھیل», so it is not shown to be less figurative than the compound; N333's rule stands that a plainer phrase needs its own evidence through the line. (4) The termbase entry «نشیب و فراز» carries ar «تضاريس» and en 'terrain, relief', and zh, de and ru name the same object (地形图, Geländekarte, Карта рельефа). So the sourced entry is not replaced on taste (P24/P25); no base amendment is made, and none is asked of the owner. The cost is charged: nativeness -5 and fit -2 on tmap.title and tmap.open (92), with «زمین کے» anchor kept, the lead right below (Jabal Al-Qarah, palm groves, dunes) and the eyebrow «سیاحتی معلومات» fixing the reading.

source_defects.defect: The form and the thank-you page say nothing about whether a reply comes or when (the label offers 'if you would like a reply'), and the note says 'none of it is published' without saying what happens to the email. Reader #25, #26, #30. The Urdu keeps faith; no promise of a reply, a period or a use of the email was added.

The toggle labels are bare noun phrases ('3D view' / '2D view') and the template shows the label of the other mode, so a reader cannot tell whether a label names the view now on or the view a press leads to (reader #51). A verb or a state word would be a change of the source and the template.

The English hints say only 'Ctrl + scroll' / '⌘ + scroll' (no direction, no wheel); the Arabic Windows hint names the mouse wheel and its Mac hint does not (stage 4, divergence 2). Reader #50 could not tell scroll from pan.

The page lists six of the twelve components, with numbers that skip (1563-004 … 1563-012), and the other six are named nowhere (reader #3, #5). Neither source explains the gaps; the sentence 'in the order of their component numbers' is all they say.

A fourth reader repeats published Urdu already on the owner's list (open item published-ur-labels-flagged): «آبی اجسام» in the lake summary (#13) and «حساوی لیموں کا باغ» under «زرعی فارم» (#47). Nothing in this batch changes them.
